messages.subject: Combining F2 population geno/pheno data
parts:
Karl & Rqtl Discussion Group:

 

I have 48 selectively genotyped (decile extremes) F2 populations (of about 220+ each).  All F2 individuals were phenotyped in each pop.  These 48 F2 pops originated from matings of a high-seed-protein inbred plant introduction (PI) with a (common) low-seed-protein elite inbred hub parent of the same maturity.

 

It now appears that in eight of the 48 matings, the differently named plant introductions (as listed in the germplasm bank) used a parents are actually identical to each other in terms of the SNP genotype.  Thus, I have eight *.csv files that could be read into Rqtl as eight F2 components of JUST ONE cross. 

 

How would I go about doing that input with a read.cross argument?  I would add that there are a few SNP markers that are present in some but absent in other populations (due to genotype calling software), so it would be somewhat tedious to try to composite the eight *.csv files into one *.csv file.  In the read.cross argument, I also would need to generate a consecutive but unique F2 ID number system for the combined 8-popuation (8 x ~220 F2) phenotype data. 

 

Are there any caveats I should be aware of in combining F2 populations, even if I am 100% confident that the 8 PI parents are identical in genotype, given that there would be some systematic (pop-specific) missing SNP marker genotype data in the combined F2 phenotypic data)?  AND what  caveats would apply with respect to combining (what would be) pop-specific F2 pop decile extremes for a combined selective genotyping analysis?   

 

If anyone has or can provide some read.cross code appropriate for my above situation of combining data, I would greatly appreciate receiving it.  I don’t have a lot of experience with R per se so I tend to end up with inelegant R coding by empirical trial and error, which takes some time to do.  That said, I  very much like Rqtl programming abilities over all, and exceptionally like it when it comes to selectively genotyped populations where stratified permutation is available!   

 

Thanks

 

Jim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Combining F2 population geno/pheno data
parts:
For this sort of data management task, I would generally write scripts in Perl (which is great for manipulating text files). Most people are now using Python; Ruby is widely recommended.

But for just the part about reading the data for the eight crosses into R and combining them, I would do something like this:

files <- c("myfile1.csv", "myfile2.csv", "myfile3.csv", [ etc ])
crosses <- vector("list", length(files))
for(i in 1:length(files))
crosses[[i]] <- read.cross("csv", file=files[i])

For combining them, I would do:

combined <- crosses[[1]]
for(i in 2:length(files))
combined <- c(combined, crosses[[i]])

I would generally include cross indicators as a set of additive covariates, to allow for shifts in the phenotype. I'd set it up like this:

n.ind <- rep(0, length(crosses))
for(i in 1:length(crosses))
n.ind[i] <- nind(crosses[[i]])

X <- matrix(0, ncol=length(crosses)-1, nrow=sum(n.ind))
cur <- n.ind[1]
for(i in 2:length(crosses)) {
X[cur + 1:n.ind[i], i-1] <- 1
cur <- cur + n.ind[i]
}

I don't think there are any special concerns about having the selective genotyping done in a stratified way.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Combining F2 population geno/pheno data
parts:
The c.cross function inserts a few extra phenotypes that are simply indicators of which individuals come from which cross. If you call c.cross repeatedly, to combine multiple crosses, you'll end up with lots of such extra phenotypes. You can ignore these.

karl
